subject: Post-call: Axion BioTech — streaming jitter, peering & VPN preflight
messages:
From: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@axionbio.com>
To: soojin.lee@redwood.ai
Cc: priya@axionbio.com, neteng@axionbio.com
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: streaming jitter and peering constraints (Axion BioTech)

Thanks for the call earlier — quick recap and concrete asks so we can prioritize the tech run. High level: we run a live inference feature that opens persistent streaming connections from devices in our US-WEST fleet into a Redwood private deployment behind a VPC peering. Recent load tests showed intermittent >200ms p95 tail on streaming responses and increased rebuffering when concurrency climbs above ~350.

Primary goals and constraints:
- Target SLOs: p50 < 60ms, p95 < 120ms end-to-end (client -> model -> client) for streaming tokens once steady-state (exclude cold-starts).
- Concurrency: target sustained 500 concurrent streaming sessions; burst up to 900 for short windows (~2 minutes).
- Throughput: average tokens/session ~1,200 over a session lifetime; typical burst token rate ~60 tokens/sec per session.
- Network path: primary via VPC peering into our us-west-2 VPC; fallback via IPSec VPN to our on-prem stack.
- Requirements: packet loss <0.1% and RTT added by peering <25ms one-way ideally. MTU must support 1500 for frame-aware batching; avoid fragmentation.

What we can share immediately: a 10-minute traffic sample (attached: axion-traffic-sample.csv) and a topology diagram (attached). Next steps we need from Redwood:
1) A short preflight checklist of tests you want us to run (tcpdump/traceroute, expected egress IPs, port ranges).
2) Proposed SLO validation plan for the tech run (what metrics you'll capture, acceptable thresholds and rollbacks).
3) Availability windows for a 2-hour tech run next week (we prefer US mornings).

Thanks — looping in NetEng. Priya or NetEng, feel free to add specifics about peering configs.

--
Tom Reilly
Senior Product Manager, Axion BioTech
---
Attachments: axion-traffic-sample.csv, axion-topology-diagram.pdf

From: soojin.lee@redwood.ai <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Tom Reilly <tom.reilly@axionbio.com>
Cc: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 07 Apr 2027 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming jitter and peering constraints (Axion BioTech)

Appreciate the clear recap and the samples, Tom — this is very actionable. Internal note: copying Karthik and Vanessa to coordinate the tech run and peering details.

Summary of our proposed approach (short):
- Preflight checklist: request the following artifacts from Axion before the run: traceroute from a set of representative client regions, tcpdump (10-min) for a problem window, advertised ASN and BGP details for peering, and the NAT/egress IPs you expect Redwood to see. See our attached redwood-net-preflight-checklist.pdf for specifics.
- SLO validation plan: we'll instrument end-to-end synthetic sessions plus server-side token-latency traces. Metrics we will capture: token emit latency (per-token), stream RTT (client-facing), p50/p95/p99 latency, reconnect rate, and packet loss derived from tcpdump. For this discovery run we'll mark cold-starts separately and focus on steady-state.
- Topology & fallback: we recommend primary VPC peering with BGP advertisement (so we can avoid NAT where possible) and IPSec VPN as a fallback path. We'll also request a short BGP session test to validate route symmetry and AS_PATH.
- Test window: propose two options for a 2-hour tech run next week: Tue 2027-04-13 09:00-11:00 PT or Thu 2027-04-15 08:00-10:00 PT. Please confirm preference.

Action items for Axion (from our side):
- Share traceroute + representative client IP ranges (needed by Fri 2027-04-09 17:00 PT)
- Confirm which egress IPs Redwood should allow on your firewall
- Sign test consent so we can source traffic generators from our side if needed

We'll use the run to validate stream tail latency at your 500 concurrent baseline and exercise the VPN fallback to observe degradation patterns. If the p95 exceeds 120ms, we'll capture packet captures and run a hop-by-hop latency analysis to identify where buffering/requeueing occurs.

I'll follow up with a lightweight runbook and internal owners.

Best,
Soojin Lee
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.ai <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 08 Apr 2027 09:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: streaming jitter and peering constraints (Axion BioTech)

Thanks — quick internal/addendum note:
- On peering: if Axion can accept our advertised routes (no NAT), that will remove one variable (NAT timeouts, asymmetric egress) — ask them to confirm whether BGP peering with route acceptance is possible.
- MTU & fragmentation: confirm MTU 1500 end-to-end; if the customer's edge performs jumbo frames we still need to make sure intermediate NAT/CFW doesn't fragment.
- Concurrency mapping: for the load we should pre-configure batching windows and an initial kv-cache warmup stage to avoid cold-step spikes. We'll run a short warmup for ~10 minutes at 60% of target concurrency before hitting 500 sustained.
- Ports/egress: we need a list of egress IPs for our nodes and preferred port ranges (443, 1024-65535 ephemeral for UDP flows if any).

I'll take point on the smoke tests and provide a small scripts bundle (traceroute/tcpdump/wget latency probes) by EOD Fri.

-karthik
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Looking forward to the run — please send the runbook and how you'll surface results (raw pcap + a short summary PDF).
